purpose: The FOUR-ROW FORM SMOKE of cell VERIFY-1: the arm's own bytes on four rows covering both registered populations, flown through core.flight.cli worker before the 625-row arm opens. Cell VERIFY-1 (Stage-3 board route F11, the verifier-selection probe; Stage-3 algorithm family inference-time-verification-v1, operator SELECTION). ONE contact per R01C construction row carries that row's OWN speech plus the FIVE sealed ROLL-1 Solver candidate answers for that same row, in a per-row presentation order pinned by the config, with NO delivered-answer anchor and no retrieved knowledge, and asks the frozen core to name the candidate the speech supports under a two-field contract (chosen_position, reason). The question is the ORACLE gap the offline sample-aggregation read measured over this same sealed rollout: +6.55 pp pooled SLU-F1 and +12.55 pp on the 225 score-disagreeing rows, none of which any deterministic agreement rule reached. Does the frozen core VERIFY better than it GENERATES? DESCRIPTIVE: no admission verdict, no comparator arm, no gate, nothing admitted, released or locked.

stage3_algorithm.note: VERIFY-1 is the first cell of this family and exercises the SELECTION operator only: the frozen core reads its OWN five sealed candidate answers for a row and names one, and the delivered artifact is that name. The family's SCORING operator is deliberately NOT claimed -- the cell asks for no per-candidate score, ranking or margin, so nothing in the sealed output can be read as a model-produced score. Nothing in the store, the plan's context or the sampling policy changes; the candidates are the sealed ROLL-1 rollout's own.
